hypothesis: A nonlinear max/min switch between the verified n=5 prior-art potential and a published canonical alternative can selectively alter the three residual taxi endpoint values while retaining complete-circle feasibility.
rationale: Both additive linear correction families are infeasible under the complete-circle constraints, which points to the lower-envelope operation as the relevant structural degree of freedom. The paper documents three canonical alternatives—the unifying, k+1, and Shinka forms—so combining them with the verified candidate tests a new envelope mechanism without inventing an arbitrary learned function.
expected_information_gain: Determines whether envelope switching can repair the residual mechanism in a small interpretable family. A circle-feasible switch earns full taxi evaluation; a strict improvement would trigger primary evaluation, generalization, and adversarial checks. Broad regression closes this envelope family.
method: For each of three published canonical alternatives, evaluate max(base, alternative+offset) and min(base, alternative+offset) for offsets {-4,-2,0,+2,+4}, producing exactly 30 candidates. Screen every candidate on all 6006 complete-circle edges. Evaluate on all 7,000,602 taxi edges only candidates with zero circle violations, and primary-evaluate only any strict taxi result. The base control is preserved in all screens.
metric: complete-circle violations_k and frozen circle-taxi violations_k; target is taxi violations_k < 3
metric_relation_to_true_objective: Complete-circle feasibility is a finite gate. Only a full frozen taxi count below 3 is strict finite objective improvement; finite zero violations do not prove the full k-server conjecture.

compute_budget.cpu: WSL2 direct canonical potential screen with eight workers and conditional full taxi evaluation
compute_budget.memory_intent: bounded envelope family; no evaluator or metric changes

kill_condition: Stop after the declared 30-candidate circle screen and conditional taxi screen, at 1800 seconds, or at a precise runtime failure. Do not add alternatives, offsets, or envelope operations after seeing results. If no strict taxi result exists, close this envelope family and pause k-server.

baseline_comparison.expected_relation: only a taxi count below 3 is strict improvement

previous_best_comparison.expected_relation: envelope switches are new combinations of documented canonical forms

interpretation: All 30 declared max/min envelope switches were feasible on the complete-circle control. On the full taxi metric, 15 matched the control at 3 violations, while the remaining switches regressed to 14, 17, or 588; no strict improvement was found.
what_was_learned: Combining the verified n=5 candidate with the documented unifying, k+1, and Shinka canonical alternatives does not repair the three taxi failures in the tested max/min offset family. The alternatives are often dominated on the circle and switch only on taxi states, where they either leave the residual count unchanged or regress.
recommended_next_action: Close this envelope-switch family and test the finite graph's arbitrary difference-constraint feasibility as a diagnostic; if the finite system itself is infeasible or overfit, require a new mathematically structured potential mechanism.
repetition_justification: This is a nonlinear max/min combination of distinct canonical potentials, not a coefficient perturbation, additive correction, index-matrix change, or soft-min temperature sweep.
